cues: Asked about his life, Runtu shakes his head.
Too many children, bad harvests, taxes, and everyone wanting money.
His face does not move, like a stone statue.
After he goes, the narrator and his mother count what has crushed him: many children, famines, taxes, soldiers, bandits, officials and gentry, squeezing him as dry as a mummy.
The pressure comes from the whole system.
